name: Investor risk

subjectOf.text: Crypto platforms typically launch an ICO when they have only an intangible product based on a basic crypto idea, so token holders invest in the future promise of an idea, and while that works for core infrastructure products such as Ethereum, most other platforms struggle to fulfill that promise.
subjectOf.abstract: Accordingly, token holders typically invest in the future promise of the idea associated with the platform. While that works well with core infrastructure products such as Ethereum, most other platforms struggle to fulfill that promise.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Marco Dell'Erba, Initial Coin Offerings Emerging Practices, Risk Factors, and Red Flags (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3067615
scope_conditions: crypto platforms other than core infrastructure products

subjectOf.text: ICOs provide the highest possible liquidity for investors at the very beginning of a platform's lifecycle, before the reporting, accounting, and legal infrastructure that gives the investing public assurance of underlying business success, so investors trade on very limited information and volatility of the tokens and the whole cryptocurrency market increases.
subjectOf.abstract: Because ICOs typically take place at the beginning of the lifecycle of a crypto business/platform, ICO investors typically invest - and the token exchange - on very limited information which increases volatility of the tokens and the entire cryptocurrency market.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Marco Dell'Erba, Initial Coin Offerings Emerging Practices, Risk Factors, and Red Flags (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3067615
scope_conditions: ICOs occurring at the beginning of a crypto business lifecycle

subjectOf.text: Because token offerings are built on open source code, the utility of an issued token can at any time be recreated in another token with essentially identical features at marginal cost, so investors cannot rely on the implicit promise that promoters and developers will increase the value of the acquired token rather than launch a duplicate.
subjectOf.abstract: Investors cannot rely on the implicit promise that the token promoters and their developers will increase the value of the acquired token and not create another token with identical features.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Marco Dell'Erba, Initial Coin Offerings Emerging Practices, Risk Factors, and Red Flags (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3067615
scope_conditions: token offerings based on open source software
